newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney H1 income before charges rises.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney H1 income before charges rises.

text.p: Euro Disney, operator of the Disneyland Paris theme park, said on Tuesday its operating performance improved in the first half of 1996/97, helping offset rising financial charges.

"Lease and financial charges increased by 68 million francs ($11.7 million) in the first half of 1997, principally due to the planned reduction of benefits from the 1994 financial restructuring, partially offset by lower interest rates," it said in its earnings statement.

"As the impact of this increase was substantially offset by the improved operating performance of the company, the loss before exceptional items was essentially unchanged from the prior year at 236 million francs," it said.
Euro Disney said the increase in lease and financial charges for the full year is estimated at 200 million francs.

"The fifth anniversary promotional momentum is now under way. The success of Disneyland Paris is growing as is our ability to manage the seasonal fluctuations in the business. However, growth in the high season remains vital to counter the sharp increases in financial charges," chairman Gilles Pelisson said in the statement.
Euro Disney's exceptional income shrank to 26 million francs from 61 million in the first half of 1995/96.
A Euro Disney spokesman said the 12.5 percent increase in revenues reflects improvements in operating performance which largely offset rises in financial charges.
He said the figures show steady growth in turnover and visitors in the first half, which is the low season for the theme park, and builds on the 13 percent rise in revenues in the year ago period.
Euro Disney is 39 percent owned by The Walt Disney Co .
